verdict.rationale: Mastra's docs describe a one-command agent harness that includes recurring schedules, and tool calls that run as tasks in the background. They also describe routing webhook or polling events into agent notification signals, and durable workflows that persist execution state to pause and resume. Together these cover scheduled and event-triggered background automation. Each of these is a one-line vendor claim, with no setup detail and no hands-on report. missing for 10: in-depth documentation of how schedules are configured and run, independent or hands-on corroboration of unattended background runs.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can set up automations that run autonomously in the background

citations.quote: create a general-purpose agent harness with a local workspace, shell tools, memory, task tracking, web access, and recurring schedules
Moving tool calls to tasks lets the agent keep responding while slow or expensive computations run in the background.
Subscribe agent threads to external resources and route webhook or polling events into notification signals.
Mastra uses storage to remember execution state, so workflows can pause indefinitely and resume where they left off.
